channels.channel: opening-group and proximity vectors, message half (the internal boundaries and the two external endpoints)
channels.how: every group of these commitments is a singleton, so at each of the 1,024 message positions the view is one 2(G+1) x (non-data rows) system over Fp; with the hidden data fixed to zero it is solved exactly and the view recomputed entry by entry

channels.channel: claim values (the internal boundaries and the two external endpoints)
channels.how: recomputed from the exhibited zero-data randomness and compared with the capture

channels.channel: opening-group and proximity vectors of A and H
channels.reason: their opening groups have several members, so each claim's own published value is an extra constraint; the correction step that handles it is in zk60_native_pg_pcs, whose MSG == PAD == 256 does not hold at this shape (1,024 message positions against 256 pads).  ROUND 7 removed that assumption; it is minutes of exact Fp arithmetic per bundle, not seconds, so it is opt-in (`--full-preimage`); the default gate stays a ~10 s tool and every figure of rounds 1-6 is taken at the same cost as before

what_is_computed_instead.note: A discloses 0 and H discloses 2, the public LogUp identity, with a certifying minor; that is a rank, not a preimage

channels.channel: the pad half of every published vector
channels.excluded: the masking commitment M's own opening, which is the separate CFS channel below
channels.reason: constructing it needs the Lagrange interpolation through the distinct sampled nodes and the Z_S divisibility test of zk60_native_pg_pcs, which assumes MSG == PAD; what IS computed is H-pad, the exact rank of the pad block over the distinct opened columns.  ROUND 7 removed that assumption; it is minutes of exact Fp arithmetic per bundle, not seconds, so it is opt-in (`--full-preimage`); the default gate stays a ~10 s tool and every figure of rounds 1-6 is taken at the same cost as before

channels.channel: opened column values
channels.reason: they are a function of the pads, which are not constructed here; the verifier's own column identity IS reproduced from the model on a sample of columns of every commitment, with no failures.  ROUND 7 constructs them; it is minutes of exact Fp arithmetic per bundle, not seconds, so it is opt-in (`--full-preimage`); the default gate stays a ~10 s tool and every figure of rounds 1-6 is taken at the same cost as before

channels.channel: the derived mask evaluation per slot (the terminal identity) -- the slots whose composition polynomial this gate recomputes
channels.derivation: fin_s == c_s*mask_eval_s + poly_s(vals_s), recomputed from the PUBLISHED terminals at the run's real challenges and compared with the capture's own terminal_polynomial, in every stage.  The plane index table (run.json[plane_index], stage 15) says which plane each terminal is an evaluation of; the public tables that are a function of the shape are rebuilt and checked against the capture's SHA-256

channels.channel: the derived mask evaluation per slot (the terminal identity) -- the slots whose public tables the bundle does not carry
channels.derivation: this bundle carries `public_tables_included: true`, so the eleven slots that read a fold of the public weights, the norm gains, the RoPE pair or a lookup table's values ARE evaluated: each table is checked against the capture's own length and SHA-256 and against the structure its builder gives it, and the identity holds at the run's real challenges in every stage
channels.is_it_public: yes -- every such table is a function of the PUBLIC statement (the weights, the norm gains, the RoPE constants, the exp and activation tables), so carrying it publishes nothing new

channels.channel: the hash RULE of the run: which BLAKE3 made every byte, and the four keys of a tagged profile
